messages:
support_ivy: FYI - high-priority ticket from Acme. Their production traffic from us-east is getting routed to eu-west intermittently, p95 token latency jumped to ~600ms and a few 401s showed up. Customer reports billing jump too. Can we triage? :rotating_light:

sre_dan: looking. do we have request/response headers or LB traces? any common path or proto?

support_ivy: pasted logs and a curl repro they ran: 
```
curl -v -H 'Authorization: Bearer <redacted>' \
  -H 'X-Client-Region: us-east' \
  https://api.redwood.example.com/v1/generate
```
Response had 401 then success routed to eu-west, latency ~620ms. headers in success: `x-serving-region: eu-west-1`, `x-envoy-upstream-host: envoy-eu-01`

eng_karen: interesting. can you grab the request-id and full trace for one of the 401s? also need the gateway route config, maybe a recent rollout touched egress steering.

support_ivy: request-id 8f3a2c4b. attached minimal trace from their side (last hop only) and the customer says it started after a deployment yesterday at 06:30 UTC.

alex_dev: the deploy-bot shows a config push at 06:29:24 UTC to l7-route-layer: added an egress-steer rule for a/b experiments. rollback not triggered. @sre_dan could this interact with zone affinity?

sre_dan: possible. I've seen sticky egress keys mis-evaluate when a header is missing. if X-Client-Region is optional, envoy might fall back to zone-picker that prefers lowest-cost region. that could explain eu-west steering. need to inspect the L7 header-preserve filter and cluster assignment.

eng_karen: can you run a quick reproducer using envoy local with same config? steps I usually use: 1) capture sample request with headers 2) proxy through local envoy binary with same vhost/route and `--log-level debug` 3) check `cluster_manager` selection logs.

alex_dev: doing that now. quick grep shows route rule with header "x-client-region" set as optional match AND a fallback-route that points to cluster `steer-eu` if not matched. config snippet: 
```
route:
  match:
    headers:
      - name: x-client-region
        exact_match: us-east
  route:
    cluster: steer-us
  fallback_cluster: steer-eu
```

support_ivy: customer insists header was present. could header be stripped by upstream auth proxy? they use an internal auth sidecar.

sre_dan: yes possible: auth service rewrites Authorization and may drop custom headers unless `preserve_request_headers` set. check auth filter chain for `set_current_client` or similar.

alex_dev: repro on my env: when auth filter runs before the header-preserve filter, `x-client-region` gets lost and route picks fallback. debug log: 
```
[debug] filter_chain auth: removing header x-client-region
[debug] cluster_manager: selected cluster steer-eu for request id=8f3a2c4b
```

eng_karen: that matches. two action items: 1) add a short-term guard: modify route to prefer `host`-based steering or make header match required for steer-us so we don't silently fallback; 2) long-term: ensure auth filter preserves region headers or insert a header passthrough stage.

support_ivy: customer asks for ETA. can we patch prod?

sre_dan: I can push a hotfix to make header match required for the steer-us route (tighten match) and remove fallback to steer-eu for the impacted service. would be a quick config patch, test in canary then prod. estimating 45-60m for canary+rollout.

alex_dev: created canary roll (`deploy-bot`): deploy-bot: canary started for l7-route-layer at 21:40 UTC, id cny-5632. monitor logs for `missing x-client-region` alarms.

deploy-bot: :white_check_mark: canary success after 10m; no misroutes observed in canary window. initiating staged rollout to 50% then 100%.

support_ivy: relayed ETA to customer (approx 1hr). they appreciate the update.

eng_karen: after rollout we should also add an alert on `header_strip` rate and a regression test in the e2e suite: auth sidecar + header-preserve. File an engineering ticket.

alex_dev: created ENG-1142: "Preserve client region header across auth filters + add header-strip alert". assigning to eng infra.

sre_dan: final note: we also saw a handful of 401s — likely because the auth proxy rejected token on first attempt, retried and succeeded routed to eu-west on retry. patch should stop region misroute; will follow up if auth failures persist. :thumbsup:
